description:
From the fz-kdt.120 cold review (2026-09-03, d2a5f3510), attacks A3/A4/A5/A13
in types/arrow_match.rs. collect_arrow_match descends into an arrow pattern's
parameters with the polarity FLIPPED for openness (OpenVars in 120's
prototype) but passes the SAME sigma, so a parameter witness contributes a
binding as if it were a lower bound:
  A3  reduce([a], b, (a,b)->b) :: b @ ([int], [], (any,[int])->[int]): a := int U any = any
  A13 filter(t(a), (a)->any) :: [a] @ ([int], (any)->bool): result [any], not [int]
  A4  f(a, (a)->nil) :: (a)->nil @ (int, (any)->nil): Known (any)->nil -- UNSOUND
      (the honest answer is (int)->nil, a SUPERTYPE of every legal (a)->nil;
      (any)->nil claims the produced function accepts values the callee never
      promised)
  A5  f(a, (a)->nil) :: a when a: integer @ (int, (any)->nil): Invalid -- a
      FALSE spec violation on a legal call (the bound check reads the polluted
      union)
All pre-existing (HEAD and prototype agree). Latent today: no @spec in
src/modules/runtime_library/ or fixtures2/ has an arrow in its RESULT; A13 is
a precision loss on filter/reject/take_while/drop_while/split_with whenever the
predicate's arrow has an any parameter. The arrow_match.rs module doc (~28-32,
~263-266) already claims "only the arrow's RESULT feeds the union" -- false of
the code. FIX: collection becomes polarity-aware (a negative occurrence records
an upper bound in its own map; the instantiation of a variable is the join of
its lower bounds, checked against the meet of its upper bounds; a variable
with only upper bounds instantiates to that meet in result positions). Red-
first: A4 and A5 as unit tests. Sequence: before fz-kdt.120 (so 120's doc
theorem is true of the code it lands on).
title: merge_subst_union collects an arrow parameter (an upper bound) into the same union as a return (a lower bound): a @spec variable in a contravariant result position instantiates unsoundly
